title: Monotonicity of a call bound
statement:
Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d,T,T'$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{vals}$ be a finite list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}	o\mathbb{Z}$ be an initial memory, and let $R,R'$ be predicates on an integer and a memory function. If a call to procedure $p$ on $\mathrm{vals}$ from memory $\mu$ at depth $d$ meets cost bound $T$ and postcondition $R$, if $T\le T'$, and if $R(r,
u)$ implies $R'(r,
u)$ for every output $r$ and memory $
u$, then the call meets cost bound $T'$ and postcondition $R'$.
